attempts.prompt:
Use case: compositing. Create one high-resolution portrait-card fusion using exactly two inputs. Image1 original small card is the sole authority for clothing, pose, hair, expression, light and crop. Image2 provides mascot identity and anatomy only. Transform the human anatomy into a smooth golden-yellow compact near-round mascot head and body with green-ringed black eyes and a source-matching mouth. Preserve the real source hair, including the bareheaded high receding forehead, short brown/grey side hair, and real brow hair. Retain the actual thin dark upper-lip moustache with a clean chin. Keep the gold/brown wire spectacles and the understated closed or mild source mouth expression. Maintain the grey/green open military lapels over the real pale grey/green inner shirt collar and dark green neckwear. Ensure the rounded chin immediately meets the raised and broadened existing neckline with a very short broad neck transition and minimal throat exposure. Do not create a separate yellow neck shaft, pointed V funnel, pinched collar, neck rolls, floating collar, clipping, or cream belly bib. Preserve the actual source open garment and observed inner collar and neckwear state with coherent front and rear collar overlap and contact shadow. Retain the small source-exposed muted gold/pale/red vertical fitting region at lower image-left beside the note, keeping fine engraving unknown. Do not copy large medal rows hidden by the note. Preserve the exact primary profile, roll, light, and crop. Retain the complete tilted dark frame, opaque photographic backing in its exact original color, and the attached lower-right cream note with faint indistinct upper marks and actual overlap. All solid surfaces must be opaque, with alpha only outside the complete card silhouette. Do not invent insignia, text, or accessories. Keep fine primary details indistinct and understated.
FINAL EXACT SOURCE REQUIREMENT: Strong IMAGE-LEFT near-profile, bareheaded high receding forehead with short BROWN/GREY side hair and real brow HAIR. Actual thin DARK upper-lip MOUSTACHE with clean chin, gold/brown WIRE spectacles and understated closed/mild source mouth. GREY/GREEN OPEN military lapels over real pale grey/green inner shirt collar and DARK GREEN neckwear. Keep the small source-exposed muted GOLD/PALE/RED vertical fitting region at lower IMAGE-LEFT beside note; fine engraving unknown. Do not copy large medal rows hidden by note. Preserve exact primary profile/roll, light and crop.
Retain exact primary head angle, expression, cap shape, real hair and visible clothing/decoration areas. One compact near-round yellow mascot head with a clearly ROUNDED short chin immediately contacting raised broad collar, no V-shaped lower-face funnel or yellow shaft. Do not copy the human long neck or angular jaw into mascot anatomy; fit the source collar to the compact rounded head. Preserve actual dark solid cloth and photographic backing opacity. Tiny ambiguous features remain understated; no new badge engraving or decorations hidden behind note. Image1 exact original card; Image2 mascot identity/anatomy only.
Output alpha: genuine transparent RGBA ONLY OUTSIDE the complete original framed portrait silhouette. The photographic BACKING INSIDE the frame is a required OPAQUE surface: preserve its original background color and texture behind the character all the way to the inner frame rim. Never turn the gaps between frame and character into transparent holes or a window. Keep the actual frame angle and rim. Preserve an overlapping paper note, pin or other attachment ONLY when actually visible in this exact source; otherwise do not invent one. Do not invent a new backdrop outside the whole card. Retain source clothing, hair, headgear, lighting and crop at full generated resolution. All originally OPAQUE subject surfaces must remain FULLY OPAQUE (alpha 255): yellow head/body, hair, beard, dark or black clothing, coat lapels, collar, tie, buttons and decorations. Dark cloth is colored material, not transparent background. Never fade garment interiors into semi-transparent patches, holes, white haze or see-through fabric. Keep any genuine source outer-edge alpha falloff only at that actual exterior boundary; preserve actual source transparency rather than making the subject itself translucent.
